statement: Whenever find_repeated_dna_sequences(s) returns r, every element of r has length 10, and for every byte vector w with len(w) = 10, let Occ(w) be the number of indices i such that 0 <= i, i+10 <= len(s), and w[k] = s[i+k] for every k with 0 <= k < 10. Then the number of indices q with 0 <= q < len(r) and r[q] = w is exactly 1 if Occ(w) >= 2, and exactly 0 otherwise. Equivalently, r contains exactly the distinct 10-byte contiguous substrings of s that occur at at least two distinct starting indices, each once, in arbitrary order.
preconditions: s is a DNA sequence: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is 65, 67, 71, or 84 (the ASCII codes of A, C, G, T). Lists and byte arrays are 0-indexed; len(s) and len(r) are numbers of bytes/elements.

statement: For every s satisfying the preconditions, find_repeated_dna_sequences(s) returns a result r; it does not fail by panic, out-of-bounds access, or machine-integer overflow.
preconditions: s is a DNA sequence: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is 65, 67, 71, or 84 (the ASCII codes of A, C, G, T). Lists and byte arrays are 0-indexed; len(s) and len(r) are numbers of bytes/elements.
